name: Mizraim
overview: Mizraim is a male biblical figure identified primarily as a son of Ham, as recorded in Genesis 10:6. He is noted for his role in the genealogies of the nations descending from Noah's sons. No additional tribal affiliations or special notes are provided beyond his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Mizraim' appears as a proper name in the Scriptures, specifically in Genesis 10:6. There is no provided meaning or divine origin for the name in the biblical text, so its significance is primarily genealogical.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mizraim as a son of Ham, linking him to the post-Flood genealogical framework. He is also explicitly noted as the father of Lud, Anam, Lehab, Naphtuh, Pathrus, Casluh, and Caphtor, according to Genesis 10:13-14. These relationships establish Mizraim as a patriarchal figure within the biblical nations.
scriptureSignificance: Mizraim holds significance as a foundational ancestor within the biblical account of the nations, representing the lineage from Ham through whom various peoples descended. His descendants are named in Genesis 10, highlighting his role in the spread of nations after the Flood. This genealogical placement underscores the biblical emphasis on God's providential ordering of peoples and their origins.
